order: For Ra = 1e4 and 1e5 the three-level order is dominated by the coarse mesh (N = 32), where the thermal boundary layer is only a few cells thick, so the fitted order is reported but the verdict requires all three Rayleigh numbers to clear the 1.5 floor. Where a Rayleigh-number family has fewer than three completed levels (the N = 128 runs are the long pole), the coverage gap is stated here rather than filled in.
third_level: The N = 128 level is the expensive one for every Rayleigh number (16 384 cells, tens of thousands of explicit steps). Runs that did not reach the stationarity criterion before the wall-clock budget expired are excluded from the published ladder instead of being reported as converged.
nusselt: Where a Rayleigh number misses the 3% band on its finest completed mesh, the cause is the boundary-layer resolution at that mesh (the thermal layer is O(H Ra^-1/4), i.e. 1.8 cells at N = 32 and Ra = 1e6), not the wall-flux formula, which is second order and is pinned by a separate unit test.
psi: The streamfunction extrema are compared with the de Vahl Davis values as a secondary check: the transcription is cross-checked against this solver's independently converged extrema (agreement better than 1% at Ra = 1e4) rather than re-read from the paper, so a psi mismatch is reported as a consistency warning, not as a refutation of the reference.
